# Explanation and planning page verification

These are fictional presentation samples, not application investigations or real
planning agreements. [sample-record.md](sample-record.md) is their only behavior
and decision source. The diagram backend is Beautiful Mermaid.

## Content and skill integration

A separate read-only reader compared both Markdown samples and generated HTML
with the fictional source record. The review found no unsupported implication or
material renderer loss. It checked the successful ordering, rejection and repeat
scenarios, diagram participants and transitions, decision statuses, proposed
checks, and production-handoff blockers. It did not assess browser appearance.

The explanation and planning skills already reference their templates and page
guidance. Those references now describe the purpose-specific openings, visible
walkthroughs and readiness, comparison fields, decision-status meanings, and
supporting evidence disclosure. Optional sections remain optional. Planning
agreement, source inspection, proposed checks, and executed results stay distinct;
presentation does not establish agreement or authorize implementation.

## Mechanical checks

The full Python suite passed 212 tests; the two Node diagram-renderer tests and
the namespace, reference, manifest, and installer checks passed. Focused page
and report tests passed again after removing an unreachable renderer condition.

Both new samples passed `render_page.py --check`. The PR sample was regenerated
and checked with its review contract using both Beautiful Mermaid and Mermaid.
New regression cases check visible critical sections, separate decision and
execution statuses, heading levels, long comparison fields, and rejection of
changed or misplaced structured rows. The checker compares fields with Markdown;
it does not judge their factual support.

## Browser inspection

One batched Chromium inspection and one confirmation after the heading fix
covered 1440px desktop, 390px mobile, and a 720px viewport. Checks passed for
document overflow, long comparison text, local navigation and focus, diagram
label bounds, print disclosure visibility, and offline viewing without
JavaScript. No JavaScript exceptions were observed.

Computed text contrast checks found no failures: explanation 92 desktop,
84 mobile, and 108 print elements; planning 179 desktop, 165 mobile, and 186
print elements. These counts exclude SVG labels. Screenshots were inspected for
openings, diagrams, comparisons, and mobile decision rows.

The single Impeccable scan found skipped comparison-heading levels. The renderer
now derives those levels from the owning authored heading; regression assertions
cover both new pages and the existing PR hierarchy. Its two table-wrapper padding
warnings are intentional because cells provide the inset. The em-dash advisory
concerned source-map entries. The detector was not rerun.

## Limits

No full model-driven Claude/Codex skill run, other-browser or screen-reader audit,
or real application investigation was performed. Samples establish presentation
behavior only. Installed plugin caches were not updated.

## Question and decision coverage follow-up

The samples now show question statuses, a labeled illustrative order, a supported
misconception correction, decision authority and delivery links, milestone changes,
an explicitly untested preservation matrix, and blockers tied to production work.
The template guidance also covers ready-to-resolve choices and relevant rollout
boundaries without requiring those sections in every document.

The second reader checked these additions against the fictional record and the
skill requirements. One label was misleading: Decisions needed now appeared above
choices whose evidence prerequisites were unresolved. It was changed to Next step
in Markdown and regenerated HTML. The remaining sampled claims matched their
record, including the absence of real agreements, execution, and production
readiness. The lead inspected the checker implementation and tests separately;
runtime enforcement was outside the second reader's source-check scope.

The full suite passed 216 Python tests. New failure cases cover missing question
content and targets, invalid statuses, absent decision acceptance/authority/delivery,
delivery links outside named slices, incomplete blocker rows, and Markdown-only
CLI enforcement. HTML parity checks cover question and blocker rows too. The two
diagram-renderer tests and namespace/installer checks passed; both PR diagram
backends were regenerated and checked without changing their report source.

Chromium checks passed for desktop, mobile, 720px, long fields, navigation/focus,
diagram bounds, print, and offline/no-JavaScript viewing. Question and blocker
tables were inspected at desktop and mobile widths. Computed text contrast had no
failures: explanation 125 desktop, 116 mobile, 140 print; planning 251 desktop,
236 mobile, 257 print. This browser pass preceded the narrow Next step label
correction; the regenerated page passed the mechanical checker afterward.

The new checks validate declared rows and links. They cannot discover an omitted
user question or decision, judge acceptance quality, verify authority, or establish
readiness. The skills retain those source and completeness checks. Full live skill
runs and other-browser or screen-reader audits remain unperformed.

## Portable status keys

Each sample now includes every value in the label families it uses. The shared
catalog supplies the Markdown key and HTML definitions; nearby HTML help links
open the relevant group. Question coverage and decision status remain distinct
from verification results, evidence origin, and diagram evidence.

A second reader compared all catalog families with their skill and evidence
rules, then compared the sample keys with the catalog. It found one lost detail:
Needs clarification must retain conflicting statements. That obligation was
restored, the samples were synchronized, and the reader confirmed the correction.
The PR sample's shorter existing fulfillment glossary was replaced by a link to
the complete key while retaining its fictional scope, supported by its record.

All 223 Python tests, two diagram-renderer tests, and namespace/installer checks
passed. Tests cover catalog completeness, context-specific definitions, unused
values, repeat synchronization, preservation of later sections, Markdown-only
delivery, stale-key rejection, custom HTML tables, and altered HTML meanings.
The installer includes the catalog and preserves foreign-file conflicts.

One batched Chromium inspection and one confirmation covered explanation, plan,
and PR pages at 1440px, 390px, and 720px. Help links work by keyboard, focus reaches
the selected heading, and definitions fit without horizontal overflow. The first
inspection exposed a mobile fragment-position issue after opening the disclosure;
the confirmation verified headings clear of the sticky navigation. Native
disclosures work offline without JavaScript, and print exposes the definitions.
Expanded-key text contrast had no failures: explanation 147 desktop / 137 mobile,
plan 300 / 284, PR review 372 / 358. No JavaScript exceptions were observed.

The single Impeccable scan reported table-wrapper padding warnings (the cells
provide the inset) and a PR em-dash advisory. No status-key correction was needed
for those findings. Both PR diagram backends were regenerated and checked.
These checks do not validate real application behavior or replace a screen-reader
or other-browser audit. Installed plugin caches remain unchanged.

## Matching label formatting

The key now reuses the report's status-badge classes for fulfillment, verification
results, decisions, and question coverage. Review action, evidence, and intent
labels reuse the existing chip component. Definitions and Markdown are unchanged;
the catalog comparison passed for all regenerated samples, including both PR
diagram backends.

All 37 focused label, review-report, and learning/planning tests passed, along with
the standalone reading-page checks. Chromium checks passed for all three sample
types at desktop and mobile widths, including contrast, navigation/focus, print,
and offline/no-JavaScript access. Desktop and mobile requirement keys were viewed.
The full repository suite was not rerun for this presentation-only change.

## Shared workflow alignment — 2026-10-10

Updated the shared evidence definitions and generated label keys. The planning
sample now marks unimplemented diagram elements as proposed and links them to
the named decision. Both companions retain their existing SVG diagrams; their
markup was compared before and after this update. Source fingerprints and
mechanical checks passed. The current full Python suite passed 105 tests.

These are still fictional samples. No new application execution, browser
inspection, or live-agent workflow evaluation was performed for this update.
Earlier browser results above retain their original scope.
